_inspectorSnowReport.Report:
Friday April 10th| 5:48 a.m 

Bonjour Tremblant!

Mother Nature is keeping things interesting for our mountain crews this morning! Rain and freezing rain overnight have created icy conditions at the summit. Our teams are already hard at work to bring you the best and safest skiing conditions possible. Terrain will open progressively throughout the day as conditions improve.

We appreciate your patience and encourage you to check back here regularly for the latest updates.

Please note that the Edge side of the mountain is now closed for the season.
The Porte du Soleil chairlift is also closed for the season.

To everyone joining us today, we’re excited to have you on the mountain! Have a fantastic day, ski safely, and enjoy every run—it’s Friday, after all!

Mountain safety tip of the week: Assist Ski Patrol.
If you witness or are involved in an accident, remain at the scene and provide your identification to ski patrol.
When you see our patrollers or safety staff responding on the slopes, slow down and make sure to give them space by staying at least 5 metres away from the incident area.

Snow fall is recorded daily at 5 a.m from mid-mountain at North Side (550 m / 1,800 ft). This data, based on 24 hours, provides a picture of on-mountain conditions. Actual accumulation may differ from the official report. Be aware of changing conditions. Lifts and trails exist in a mountain environment and may close due to weather, usage and/or special maintenance.
